test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: general
question: ABC is a right angle triangle and angle ABC = 90 degrees. BD is a perpendicular on the side AC. What is the value of BD² ?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse divides the triangle into two similar triangles.

According to the Right Triangle Altitude Theorem (Geometric Mean Theorem):

The square of the altitude (BD) is equal to the product of the segments of the hypotenuse (AD and DC).

BD² = AD × DC

**∴ The correct answer is AD × DC.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ABC is a right-angled triangle where ∠ABC = 90° and BD ⊥ AC.

**Formula Used:** Similarity of triangles (AA criterion) and ratio of corresponding sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/956e9fc4f42bd3dff36256dd1931b66e651925e1009345145fe8494ce235b1fc.png] 

⇒ In ▵ABD and ▵BCD:

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠BDC = 90° (Since BD ⊥ AC)

⇒ ∠BAD = 90° − ∠ABD (In ▵ABD)

⇒ ∠CBD = 90° − ∠ABD (Since ∠ABC = 90°)

⇒ ∴ ∠BAD = ∠CBD

⇒ By AA Similarity, ▵ABD ∼ ▵BCD

⇒ Corresponding sides are in proportion: BD/AD = DC/BD

⇒ Cross-multiplying: BD × BD = AD × DC

⇒ BD² = AD × DC

**∴ The correct answer is AD × DC.**

**__Additional Information__**

Leg Rule in Right Triangles

The square of a leg is equal to the product of the hypotenuse and the segment of the hypotenuse adjacent to that leg: AB² = AD × AC and BC² = CD × AC.

Area-Altitude Relationship

The product of the legs of a right triangle is equal to the product of the hypotenuse and the altitude to the hypotenuse: AB × BC = AC × BD.

Reciprocal Property

The reciprocal of the square of the altitude is equal to the sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the legs: 1/BD² = 1/AB² + 1/BC².</p
